summary: On Friday, October 20, 2023, House Republicans dropped Rep. Jim Jordan as their nominee for speaker in a closed-door session after he lost a third floor ballot, losing 25 GOP votes. The decision deepened a crisis that has shut down the House since Kevin McCarthy was ousted at the start of the month. No Republican currently appears able to win a majority, and options such as empowering interim Speaker Patrick McHenry face resistance from hard-liners.
one_line: House Republicans dumped Jim Jordan as speaker nominee after a third failed ballot, prolonging the leadership crisis that began with Kevin McCarthy's ouster.
key_facts: Republicans dropped Rep. Jim Jordan as their House speaker nominee on Friday in a closed-door session after he failed on a third ballot.
Jordan said of his colleagues, "We put the question to them, they made a different decision."
In the third floor vote, Jordan lost 25 Republican colleagues, worse than the 20 and then 22 he lost in earlier rounds that week.
Friday's vote was 194 for Jordan, his lowest tally yet, and 210 for Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, with two absences on each side.
Republicans hold a 221-212 House majority, and a candidate needs 217 votes to become speaker.
Majority Leader Steve Scalise said Republicans would "come back and start over" on Monday.
The House has been shut down for more than two weeks since hard-liners ousted Kevin McCarthy at the start of the month.
An idea to give interim Speaker Pro Tempore Patrick McHenry more powers was rejected by Jordan's allies, with Rep. Jim Banks calling it a "betrayal."
Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks said she received "credible death threats" after voting against Jordan on the second ballot.
The stalemate could last until the mid-November deadline for Congress to approve funding or risk a federal government shutdown.
Jordan relied on backing from Donald Trump and outside pressure groups, which backfired on some lawmakers.
Jordan, first elected in 2006, is a founding member of the House Freedom Caucus, has few bills to his name, and received a Medal of Freedom from Trump days after the Jan. 6 attack.
